hypothesis: Every past variant (feature widening, L2 sweep, deeper architectures, multi-task, popularity reweighting, ensembling) has shown the same early-peak-then-degrade overfitting signature under a fixed bilinear-interaction capacity — none has touched the actual *encoding* of the highest-cardinality fields (user_id, video_id, author_id), which likely have a long tail of very-low-frequency ids whose embeddings get memorized/noisy rather than learned. I'll add a frequency-threshold fallback in data.py's encode(): any user_id/video_id/author_id value appearing fewer than `min_count` times in train gets collapsed into one shared "RARE" bucket per field (distinct from the existing cold-start UNK bucket for values never seen in train at all), reducing effective embedding-table capacity exactly where it's noisiest while leaving frequent-id embeddings untouched.
reflection: The DeepFM+FM ensemble underperformed both standalone models (0.6033 vs 0.6041) and its own training curve degraded after epoch 4 — consistent with the overfitting signature every mechanism so far has shown; averaging two overfit-prone scorers didn't fix the underlying capacity/regularization issue. Per the plateau warning, I should try an untried lever rather than another variant of ensembling/architecture/training-loss changes.
expected_effect: GAUC should move more than nDCG@5, since denoising the tail of the user_id/video_id/author_id embedding tables should generalize better across the broad population of users/rows that GAUC aggregates over, while nDCG@5 is already near-saturated for the majority of users with <5 valid rows (per the node-10 probe) regardless of embedding quality.
